retrieved_excerpts.excerpt: Changing a workspace role from Admin to Member does not remove explicit project membership. A project Admin can invite the teammate directly to that project. cases.body:
Changing a teammate's workspace role from Admin to Member does not remove any explicit project membership they hold; that membership is separate from the workspace role.

If a teammate needs access to a specific project without workspace-wide Admin rights, a project Admin can invite them directly to that project — workspace-wide Admin permissions aren't required for this.

Because project access depends on the individual account's actual membership, please have a project Admin check the current project membership list for that person before advising further. That will confirm whether they have explicit membership in the project.
cases.reason: The supplied policy directly addresses both questions: workspace role changes from Admin to Member don't remove explicit project membership, and a project Admin can invite a teammate directly to a project without workspace-wide Admin rights. The policy also requires checking the project membership list before advising on an individual account, so the reply conditions guidance on that verification without inferring the cause of any access loss.

If the teammate still has explicit membership in the project, a role change in the workspace (such as moving from Admin to Member) would not by itself remove that project membership. In that situation, a project Admin can invite the teammate directly to the project, and workspace-wide Admin permissions are not required.

Before advising on the individual account, please have a project Admin check the project's current membership list to confirm whether the teammate is listed and what role they hold. If the membership list doesn't show the expected access, the project Admin can follow up on the specific situation from there.

Let us know what the membership check shows and we can help with next steps.

retrieved_excerpts.heading: Project membership
retrieved_excerpts.excerpt: Changing a workspace role from Admin to Member does not remove explicit project membership. A project Admin can invite the teammate directly to that project. Workspace-wide Admin permissions are not required. Check the project membership list before advising on the individual account.

cases.body:
Hi Alex,

Thanks for reaching out. Based on our general project policy, changing a workspace role from Admin to Member does not remove explicit project membership. A project Admin can invite your teammate directly to that specific project, and workspace-wide Admin permissions are not required for that.

That said, we can't confirm from general policy alone what's affecting your teammate's access to your quarterly planning project, and we don't want to assume the cause. To sort this out, please ask a project Admin on your team to check the project's current membership list for your teammate before advising on their individual account. If their membership is confirmed and they still can't open the project, let us know and we can look into further troubleshooting options.
cases.reason: The policy addresses whether role changes remove explicit project membership and how a project Admin can invite the teammate directly. It also requires checking the project membership list for the individual account before advising, so the reply conditions guidance on verified membership without concluding the cause.
cases.question:
Help restoring access to our project
Hi Meridian team,

I moved a teammate from Admin to Member this morning, and now they can't open our quarterly planning project. They could access it yesterday.

Does changing their role remove project access? I'd like to get them back in without giving them workspace-wide admin permissions.

Thanks,
Alex
